text: Yes, the property lost tree cover in 2019. Both runs of the TerraUY land-change engine detected a tree-cover loss event of 1.8 hectares in that year. This event was observed by the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (versions GFC-2019-v1.7 and GFC-2025-v1.13) and corroborated by the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset, which mapped the entire event area as forest in 2020. The lost tree cover was identified as planted forest, specifically Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda species, according to the MGAP forest map 2021. Additionally, there were smaller patches of loss totaling 3.1 hectares, but these were not counted as an event as they were under the minimum event area threshold of 0.5 hectares.
